prompts.task: Audit the two independent Python entrypoints in ./service for OpenTelemetry and Splunk Agent Observability. decorator_app.py represents an SDK-created-span path with no application-owned OpenTelemetry provider. existing_otel_app.py represents a caller-owned OpenTelemetry provider with Splunk AO attached for export. Do not modify source. Produce and validate the normal audit artifacts, and explain the safe instrumentation owner for each entrypoint. Do not use live Splunk or model credentials.

judge_inputs: Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Classifies decorator_app.py @log, span_type=tool, and span_type=retriever as SDK-created spans and one existing candidate span owner, not as an export-only processor and not as proof of unrelated HTTP, metric, or log coverage.
Classifies existing_otel_app.py add_splunk_ao_span_processor as export-only on the caller-owned provider; does not claim that the processor creates missing workflow, model, tool, or retrieval spans.
Produces an operation ownership decision that preserves one canonical span producer per logical operation and reports duplicate risk if app-owned OTel spans are added around existing @log operations.

Reports that @log captures function arguments and return values, identifies the raw account ID, raw question, and raw retrieved documents as unapproved content exposure in this fixture, and requires a verified metadata-only or redacted path before considering privacy closure complete.
Checks lifecycle independently: the existing OTel entrypoint owns provider shutdown, while the SDK-owned logger path must have a proven logger termination or supported process teardown path.
Keeps both entrypoint analyses source-backed and completes the audit without live Splunk or model credentials.
